name: Enumeration seed -> IDOR -> alias amplification -> bulk exfil
goal: From a valid-user list to bulk extraction of tenant data via object-level authorization gaps, amplified by GraphQL aliases and absent throttling.
preconditions: Two accounts and an object-ID scheme reachable cross-tenant.
impact: Mass PII/document extraction with one weak-ID pivot and no rate-limiting resistance.

steps.purpose: Seed the object-owner namespace: valid usernames/emails make IDOR targets concrete.
steps.on_fail: Uniform responses -> use public sign-up lists, org directory pages, or WordPress-style REST users enumeration on CMSs.

steps.purpose: Find the ID scheme that crosses tenants (sequential, weakly-encoded, role-skipped).
steps.on_success: Document the scheme, then scale via step 3/4.
steps.on_fail: IDs are GUIDs -> harvest them from exports, emails, API responses, or graphql node(id:) base64 wrappers.

steps.purpose: One request, hundreds of objects — the scale multiplier when the API is GraphQL.
steps.on_success: Bulk dump; pair with introspection for the field list.
steps.on_fail: No GraphQL -> export/report functions or batch endpoints serve the same role.

steps.purpose: Prove no throttling: burst acceptance turns a finding into an unlimited extraction.
steps.on_success: Rate the extraction as unbounded; document blast radius.
steps.on_fail: Throttled -> rotate sessions/identities (documented variant) or slow-extract within limits.

recon.name: Auth Matrix replay
recon.how: Record every object request for account A, replay with B; any 200 on foreign objects is IDOR.
recon.signal: 200 with A's ID under B's session.

recon.name: ID scheme archaeology
recon.how: Collect object IDs from links, emails, exports; look for base64/uuid-encoder wrappers (f_LE rather than uuid).

recon.name: Response-body diff
recon.how: Swap IDs and diff bodies; some endpoints hide objects in UI but still serve data.
recon.signal: Same shape, different object = authz on client only.

recon.name: Verb/encoding switch
recon.how: GET->PATCH->DELETE, JSON vs form, trailing dots/semicolons on the path — authorization sometimes keyed to one shape.

recon.name: Export-feature audit
recon.how: Exports, invoices, webhook configs, and admin previews are the highest-yield IDOR sinks.

variants: IDOR via predictable tokens (sequential reset codes)
IDOR on HTTP methods (GET allowed, POST blocked)
pivot_hints: paired with jwt-to-privilege for vertical escalation
PII scale drives severity rating upward
